beats: Hook (Q25-02 10:31-12:52, slide p9): the textbook oscillator, a mass on a spring (in circuit form a capacitor and a coil), climbs in equal energy steps, so a pulse that lifts it from 0 to 1 lifts it on from 1 to 2 and beyond (line_qc_spring_bounce). What one strange part fixes it? Cast for the hardware half of QC02: the technician (short wavy hair, small square glasses, a lab coat).

Where the chip lives: a manufactured circuit at the bottom of a very cold refrigerator (line_qc_fridge_chandelier, drawn generically, no maker). The lecture gives no temperature: any figure goes through FACTS.md first.
Reading a quantum program (p4, 05:29-07:15): wires are qubits, boxes gates, meters measurements, double lines classical bits; read left to right (code draws the circuit; reuse line_scroll_reader).

The transmon (p9): a Josephson junction plus a capacitor; the junction makes the steps uneven (the 0-1 gap larger than the 1-2 gap), so a pulse tuned to 0-1 no longer fits 1-2 and the qubit stays in 0 and 1. A swing pushed in its small-swing rhythm stays low, because its rhythm changes as it swings higher (line_qc_swing_two_beats). On-screen caveat: the swing pictures the uneven spacing; the levels themselves are quantum. Clip Q25-02 11:54-12:25.
Why only two levels (14:44-15:43): qutrits and qudits exist, but the cost outweighs the benefit (code: levels 0, 1, 2, 3 on the taped p9; no drawing).

Built, not found (17:51-18:38, clip 17:51-18:21): a superconducting qubit is a manufactured, artificial atom; ion-trap and neutral-atom machines use natural atoms (line_qc_built_vs_found; the ion chamber is generic).

Single-qubit gate (p10, 18:38-21:29): a shaped microwave pulse at the qubit's own frequency, through a nearby line; only what is tuned to that pitch answers (line_qc_tuning_fork_glasses). Ions and atoms: "often lasers".
Two-qubit gate (p11, 22:02-25:24): a resonator must sit between the pair; no resonator, no gate (line_qc_tin_can_houses).

So the wiring fixes which pairs can ever interact: the 5-qubit chip's coupling graph (p14, redrawn, credit Murali et al. 2019) as a village of string phones, the middle cottage linked to all four corners plus the left pair and the right pair (line_qc_string_village; again in QC02-02 and QC02-04). Chip micrographs on p8-p12 are covered.

Measurement (p12, 25:27-27:36): read through a neighbouring resonator, never by looking at the qubit itself (line_qc_bell_beside_box); 0 with probability |alpha|^2, 1 with |beta|^2 (code draws two bars; reuse line_dice_hand only for "a random outcome"). Her cat-in-a-cage aside is not drawn.

Her wave picture (26:31-27:05): waves from many sources add up strongly at some points and cancel at others (line_qc_ripple_tank); quantum amplitudes interfere in the same way, which is how algorithms push the odds toward the right answer (the math comes in QC04).

Takeaway (27:36-28:12, clip): this much physics is enough for system design; from QC02-02 on, the chip is a dinner table (chairs = physical qubits, guests = program qubits, the head waiter = the compiler).
Cover (line_qc_cover_qc02_01; for the X post and thumbnails, not a film beat): the spring weight bouncing wildly beside the technician's calm push on a swing.
